definitions.definition: An instance of exhibiting, or something exhibited.
A large-scale public showing of objects or products.
A public display, intentional or otherwise, generally characterised as negative.

quote.citation: 2002, George Harrison (lyrics and music), “Stuck Inside a Cloud”, in Brainwashed:
quote.text: Well I made some exhibition, I lost my will to eat / The only thing that matters to me is to touch your lotus feet

definitions.definition: A demonstration of personal skill or feelings.

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter XV, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume II, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 178:
quote.text: "I could not have believed," remarked Francesca, "had I not witnessed it since my residence in your country, how the reality and the affectation of feeling can exist together. Before I left our solitary home, the very exhibition of emotion would have tempted me to doubt its truth. Now, I observe that some affect, as others shun, display; yet the feeling is equally true in both."

definitions.definition: (UK) A financial award or prize given to a student (who becomes an exhibitioner) by a school or university, usually on the basis of academic merit.

quote.citation: 1978, Lawrence Durrell, Livia (Avignon Quintet), Faber & Faber, published 1992, page 352:
quote.text: He was a scholarship boy who had won an Exhibition to Oxford, and then, like so many others, had found himself thrown upon the slave market of pedagogy.

quote.citation: 2016 November, Jonathan Meades, “Inside Job”, in Literary Review:
quote.text: Despite a couple of rustications, he gained an exhibition to Cambridge.

definitions.definition: (sports) A game which does not impact the standings for any major cup or competition.
